ui.title: Own build
ui.tagline: Every night, the files the specs promise are checked against the files in the repository and the files Kiro worked on.

intended.label: Specs
intended.source: The file paths and folders written in backticks in .kiro/specs design, tasks and requirements files, read from a recorded snapshot. A relative path names the one tracked file it ends, a folder names every tracked file under it, and build output is left out. A path that ends no tracked file, or more than one, is kept as written and shows as promised and never built.

observed.label: Repository
observed.source: The files git tracks at one recorded commit.

billed.label: Kiro work
billed.source: The files Kiro worked on, summed across sessions. The amount is Kiro credits, not money, and the page prints it with a dollar sign. Each session's credits are split equally across the files it touched. That split is an allocation chosen for this audit, not a measurement. A blank share counts as zero and the line stays.

unkeyed.explanation: A Kiro record that names no file cannot be matched to the specs or the repository, so it is kept apart.

notes.text: Credits per file are an allocation: each session's credits are split equally across the files it touched. They are not a measurement of what one file cost.
Some Kiro sessions were stopped before they reported credits, so their files carry zero credits and stay on the list.

A path in a spec is resolved against the files git tracks: the one tracked file it ends, or every tracked file under a folder. A path that ends no tracked file, or more than one, is kept as written, so it shows as promised and never built.
Some credits were spent in sessions that touched no file, so no file carries them.
